Subject: Initial privacy intake and DPA request

Hi Jonas —

We're kicking off onboarding for a pilot integration between CloudFlow and Redwood (data processing for observability traces and user metadata). Can you please: 1) share Redwood's standard privacy/addendum template, 2) provide a current subprocessors list (or attestation process), and 3) confirm whether you support DocuSign or AdobeSign for execution?

We also need clarity on cross-border transfer mechanisms for EU customers (SCCs or other lawful basis). Timelines: CloudFlow legal would like a signed addendum before the start of the pilot on Aug 16.

I've attached our internal intake form for context (CloudFlow_DPA_Request_v1.docx). Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Natalie Green
Head of Security & Privacy
CloudFlow

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Hi Natalie —

Thanks for the intake doc — appreciate the clear scope. Attaching Redwood's privacy annex template and a simple dataflow diagram showing what fields are processed. High-level answers in-line below.

On Sun, 19 Jul 2026 at 09:12, Natalie Green <natalie@cloudflow.com> wrote:
> We're kicking off onboarding for a pilot integration between CloudFlow and Redwood (data processing for observability traces and user metadata). Can you please: 1) share Redwood's standard privacy/addendum template, 2) provide a current subprocessors list (or attestation process), and 3) confirm whether you support DocuSign or AdobeSign for execution?
>
> We also need clarity on cross-border transfer mechanisms for EU customers (SCCs or other lawful basis).

Responses:
- Template: attached (redwood_privacy_annex_template_v1.docx).
- Subprocessors: we publish a real-time subprocessor page publicly, and we can provide a snapshot export for contracting. For onboarding, we can do either: (a) provide the current list + 30-day notice for changes, or (b) provide an attestation plus monthly updates — let us know preference.
- E-sign: default is DocuSign (we have an enterprise account). We can accommodate AdobeSign if required by procurement but DocuSign is faster for our flow.
- Transfers: for EU->US transfers we use EU SCCs with our supplementary data processing terms; Private deployments can avoid cross-border transfers entirely.

Questions for CloudFlow:
- Which CloudFlow BU/legal entity will sign?
- Will you require prior disclosure of all subprocessors or is attestation acceptable for pilot?
- Expected signing timeline (you mentioned Aug 16 start).

Next steps: if DocuSign is fine, I can prepare an execution packet and a preview link. Attaching: redwood_privacy_annex_template_v1.docx, dataflow-cloudflow.png

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0119

Subject: Re: Initial privacy intake and DPA request — Redwood legal notes and proposed timeline

Hi Natalie, Jonas —

Laura from Redwood Legal here — looping in to manage redlines and to propose an execution cadence.

On Jonas' helpful note: we generally handle the following items in the privacy annex / DPA for pilots: subprocessors, SCC incorporation, data retention windows, and audit rights. To keep things efficient for pilot customers we offer: (1) our standard annex with limited negotiated fields (retention, contact points, and subprocessor disclosure cadence), and (2) a quick-track DocuSign flow for pilot-level agreements.

Key asks for CloudFlow to confirm:
- Legal entity that will sign (full corporate name + jurisdiction).
- Whether CloudFlow requires prior written approval of each subprocessor (we typically provide attestation + 30 days notice; prior-approval is reserved for sensitive categories).
- Any required changes to the SCC insertion (our standard SCC text can be included).

Proposed timeline:
- CloudFlow returns any redlines by EOD Mon Jul 26.
- Redwood legal reviews and responds within 2 business days.
- If redlines are material, we'll schedule a 30-minute call to resolve.

If DocuSign is acceptable we'll prepare the packet and send a preview link for review before execution.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
